title: A Pantry for Big Flavours
excerpt: The ten ingredients we always keep in the cupboard, and how each one turns an ordinary weeknight dinner into something worth sitting down for.

body.text: Big flavour rarely comes from complicated recipes. It comes from a handful of hard-working ingredients used with confidence. Keep these in the cupboard and you are never more than half an hour from a dinner you're proud of.
Keep two kinds: fine sea salt for seasoning as you cook and flaky salt for finishing. Seasoning early and in layers makes food taste more of itself, not saltier.

A good extra virgin olive oil for finishing, a neutral oil for searing, unsalted butter and, if you roast often, a jar of beef dripping or goose fat. Fat carries flavour; choosing the right one is half the dish.
Lemons, red wine vinegar, Dijon mustard and chilli flakes. When something tastes flat, it almost always needs acidity rather than more salt. A squeeze of lemon at the end can wake up an entire pan.
Tomato purée, Worcestershire sauce, good stock and a hard cheese like Parmesan. These are your shortcuts to savoury depth, the backbone of ragùs, braises and gravies.
When a dish tastes flat, reach for acid before you reach for salt.
